articleBody:
A shower niche provides clean, built-in storage, but placing one improperly can compromise wall insulation, hit plumbing vents, or create water pooling. Use this checklist to plan your shower storage before backer board and waterproofing go up.

- [ ] Measure your tallest shampoo and body wash bottles — Ensures the shelf height leaves ample clearance without tipping bottles forward.
- [ ] Inspect existing wall cavity depth — Verifies whether standard 2x4 studs provide the necessary finished depth or if blocking must be modified.
- [ ] Check for hidden vent pipes and electrical lines — Avoids costly disruptions that occur when cutting blindly into existing bathroom wall cavities.
- [ ] Avoid placing niches on exterior walls — Keeps exterior insulation intact to prevent interior condensation and cold spots during Utah winters.
- [ ] Select a preformed waterproof niche or structural backer — Guarantees precise square corners and an engineered surface ready for waterproofing membranes.
- [ ] Plan horizontal shelf slope toward the shower drain — Prevents soapy water from pooling on the bottom sill and degrading grout lines.
- [ ] Align niche boundaries with surrounding tile layout — Minimizes awkward thin tile slivers and preserves full tile patterns across the wall.
- [ ] Secure waterproof sealing tape along all outer perimeter seams — Creates a continuous, watertight connection between the niche flange and surrounding wall backer.

### How to Use This Checklist
